question: ***Which racecourse in Paris*** hosts the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe, the most prestigious race in French horse racing?
***Which vitamin*** is commonly recommended as a supplement during pregnancy to reduce the likelihood of neural tube defects such as spina bifida?
explanation: FOLATE (or vitamin B9, FOLACIN, FOLIC ACID)

question: ***Which battle***, often dubbed the bloodiest to have ever occurred on English soil, took place in Yorkshire on 29 March 1461 and saw a Yorkist force led by Edward IV rout the forces of the House of Lancaster?
First published in 1879, The Watchtower is an illustrated magazine distributed by ***which religious group***, founded in Pennsylvania in the 1870s?
***What sort of animal*** is depicted in the 1762 George Stubbs painting Whistlejacket?
***What would be served*** in a small cup called a ‘demitasse’?
Beau Greaves is the reigning three-time women’s world champion in ***which sport***? She was not one of the two women who competed at the recent men’s world championship in this sport.
In radio frequency or RF engineering, ***how many ohms is the conventional termination impedance*** or characteristic impedance when using coaxial cables for signal transmission?
Buddy Rich and Gene Krupa were notable jazz musicians who ***played which instrument***, an integral part of a jazz rhythm section?
***Which group of aquatic flightless birds*** consists of 18 species including gentoo, chinstrap and Galapagos? They all have black plumage on the back and head and white plumage on their fronts.

George Bernard Shaw parodies himself as Captain Shotover in ***which play***, set in a nautical themed home in Sussex and inspired by the works of Chekhov?
Doing so in 1904, ***what was the first American city*** to host the Olympics?

The French colony known as French Somaliland was a predecessor to ***what modern-day African nation***? In 1967 it became the French Territory of the Afars and the Issas before adopting its current name upon independence in 1977.
***Which geological epoch***, that lasted from 2.5 million years ago to 11,700 years ago, is the first epoch of the quaternary period and is colloquially known as the ‘Ice Age’?
Named after the American Christian missionary who developed it in the 19th century, ***what romanisation system*** is widely used to transcribe the Japanese language?

***Which Conservative politician and novelist*** was sentenced to four years in prison in 2001 for perjury and perverting the course of justice?
The 1990 novel Postmortem marked the first appearance of ***which fictional forensic examiner***, created by Patricia Cornwell?

The tufted, horned and Atlantic are the three species of ***what group of small, black-and-white seabirds***? These birds have been nicknamed ‘clowns of the sea’ and ‘sea parrots’ due to their large, brightly-coloured bills, and the Atlantic species breeds around the coasts of UK and Ireland.

Often simply referred to as the ‘human slaughterhouse’, ***which prison***, just north of Damascus, was liberated after the fall of the Assad regime with over 2,000 prisoners being released? The body of notable anti-Assad activist Mazen al-Hamada was found in the prison during the liberation.
***Which mountain*** is located on the junction of Brazil, Guyana and Venezuela? It is a spectacular table-top mountain and is the highest of the Paracaraima chain.
The Sistine Madonna, The School of Athens and Transfiguration are among the notable works of ***which Renaissance painter***?

***Which sportsman*** is the only person to have played in both a Super Bowl and a World Series? He is currently head coach of the university team the Colorado Buffaloes but is widely tipped to join the NFL in a head coach role very soon.
***Which of the four main islands of Japan*** is the smallest by both area and population?

***Which spitz-type dog***, originally from northern China, is the closest relative of the shar pei, with both breeds having distinctive blue-black tongues? This breed is identified by its dense double coat that is particularly thick around the neck area.
***Which Dutch rock band*** reached number 8 in the UK singles chart in 1970 with the song ‘Venus’, which would reach number 8 once again in 1986 when covered by Bananarama?

***Which midfielder***, whose club career included spells at Sampdoria, Real Madrid and Middlesbrough, played football 53 times for France between 1992 and 2002? He is known for refusing to sing La Marseillaise before international matches, due to France’s colonial-era activity in New Caledonia, where he was born and raised.

Eventually killed in a gas chamber at Birkenau concentration camp, ***what nun*** was later canonised as a martyr and a Catholic saint? Jewish by birth, she converted to Catholicism and became a Carmelite before being arrested in 1942; she would later be named one of the patron saints of Europe.
explanation: Edith STEIN (accept TERESA BENEDICTA of the Cross)

question: Part of the Saint Mark series, the Miracle of the Slave is a painting by ***which Venetian Renaissance painter*** whose birth name was Jacopo Robusti?
